One muon through the forward fit, step by step

det3 · Saturday long run, resistive 490 V / drift 1000 V · event 1663, Y plane · calibration calib_bundle_r06 · 18 August 2026

This is the long version of deck slides 9b and 9c: the same event, but with every stage drawn — including the raw waveforms of the core strip and its ±1 and ±2 neighbours, which the slides only ever show already modelled.

Which calibration this runs on, and why it matters

Everything below uses calib_bundle_r06, in which c2 = 0.6 c1 — the ±2 copy is smaller than the ±1 copy, which is the only ordering a resistive film can produce, because the ±2 strip is reached only through the ±1 strip.

Every bundle shipped before 21 August had that backwards — det3 at c2/c1 = 1.14, det2 1.53, det7 1.75, det4 2.12 — because the reference-pinned cosmic χ² is genuinely flat in that direction, so an unconstrained fit wanders there and stays. It was retired on 21 August together with every product built on it, and wft.calib.check_kernel_ordering now refuses such a bundle at load, at save and at install. Section 10 is what that cost.

Your description, checked

“We guess a charge distribution over each strip, produce the 0, ±1, ±2 waveforms, then sum over all strips and iterate track angle to see what fits the waveforms simultaneously best.”

Right in outline, and right about the thing that matters — every strip is predicted, nothing is inverted, and one geometry has to explain the whole window at once. Three corrections:

  • The free charge is not per strip. It is per 60 ns arrival slice — 18 of them, i.e. a charge-versus-depth profile. Where each slice's charge lands on the strips is not free: it is fixed by the geometry through the strip integral. That is what makes the fit tight — 18 charges and 3 geometric numbers against 608 measurements.
  • The charges are not iterated. At every trial geometry they are solved exactly, in one step, by non-negative least squares. Only three numbers are searched: p0, w, t0.
  • The ±1 / ±2 copies are inside the prediction, not added afterwards. Each column of the design matrix already carries them, so the strip that receives a copy and the strip that donated it are fitted with one consistent set of charges.

1What comes in

19 strips × 32 samples of 60 ns, pedestal-subtracted DREAM ADC. Nothing else — no hit times, no thresholds, no reference track. The diagonal in the left panel is the drift: charge liberated near the cathode arrives last, and on an inclined track it arrives on a different strip.

2The three numbers

The model says: a straight segment crossed the 36.6 µm/ns drift gap. Cut its arrival into slices of Δt = 60 ns. Slice k arrives at t0 + uk and was liberated at transverse position p0 + w uk. Three numbers, 18 slices, and a full 30 mm drift takes 820 ns.

3Geometry decides where each slice lands

Each slice is a little cloud: its transverse extent over the 60 ns bin, widened by the initial cloud size σp0 = 0.425 mm and by transverse diffusion, integrated over the 0.78 mm pitch. That integral — strip_fractions — is the matrix Fsk. No free parameter in it that is not already calibrated.

4The resistive kernel copies charge sideways, late

The strips sit on a resistive film. Charge that spreads through it reaches the neighbour late and dispersed. In this calibration that is modelled as a delayed copy of the impulse response: amplitude c1 at a lag of τs = 166 ns to ±1, and c2 = 0.6 c1 at twice the lag to ±2 (share_mode = 'delay').

5One slice → five waveforms

This is the step your description was pointing at. Put one unit of charge in one slice and ask what the electronics record. It lands mostly on one strip (blue); the kernel copies a fraction onto ±1 (vermillion) and ±2 (purple); each of those is folded with that plane's measured impulse response. That is one column of the design matrix.

6The charges are solved, not searched

Stack those columns and you have A, 608 × 18. The prediction is A q. At each trial (p0, w, t0) the charge profile is whatever minimises ‖A q − y‖ subject to q ≥ 0 — a convex problem with one answer, no starting guess and no iteration over the charges. The non-negativity is doing real work: it is what stops the fit inventing negative charge to absorb a mismatched tail.

7What each strip’s prediction is made of

Now the same decomposition on the fitted event: for six consecutive strips, the model waveform split into the strip’s own charge, its ±1 neighbours’ copies, and its ±2 neighbours’, against the measured samples.

8The whole window at once

What this is not

It is not a χ² ≈ 1 fit. χ²/dof = 19 here, and the residual image has visible structure: the model is good to ~3 % of the peak, while the electronics noise is 0.7 % of it. So the error bars in the fit are the noise, but the residuals are dominated by model error — the impulse-response shape, the single-τ kernel, the straight line, the 60 ns binning. The parameter errors that come out of the curvature are therefore optimistic; the resolution we quote is measured against the reference (step 11), not read off the χ².

9What is actually searched

Three scans, one per searched number, plus a two-dimensional map, with everything else held at the optimum. The fit itself is a coarse grid followed by Nelder-Mead — but the scans are what the minimiser is walking on.

Two details that are easy to miss. t0 is not free. The χ² surface has near-degenerate minima one depth bin (60 ns) apart — shift the profile a bin and slide p0 by w × 60 ns and the prediction is nearly the same — and only about a third of unconstrained fits land in the physical one. A prior from the scintillator trigger phase selects it — mostly by seeding the search there rather than by out-weighing the χ², as the box in section 10 shows. Here it sits at 271 ns with σ = 5 ns. And vdrift enters exactly once, at the end: tan θ = w / v.

The w0/kw line is an honest wart: a per-plane linear map measured after the fact from free fits of reference tracks, absorbing a small residual offset and scale. The bundle ships the old kernel’s values, which are stale by construction, so the ones used here were re-measured on the 180 calibration events with bench/set_w0.py’s recipe and applied to the 220 held-out ones — never fitted on the events being scored.

10What it cost

The ±2 strip is reached only through the ±1 strip, so c2 < c1 always. Pinning the ratio and refitting everything else is a refit, not a relabelling — τs and σs move with it, and on the fleet c1 rises by roughly 1.8× while σs rises by an order of magnitude. The model compensates for the smaller ±2 copy with a wider, later ±1 copy.

It is a trade, and the deck states it as one

The corrected kernel is worse on angular resolution, on three of four planes. Paired bootstrap over identical events, superseded → corrected: det3 Y +0.061 ± 0.013° (4.7σ), det7 Y +0.131 ± 0.019° (6.9σ), det7 X +0.076 ± 0.033°; det3 X flat. The training χ² agrees — pinning the ratio anywhere in 0.45–0.8 costs 2.8–3.3 % of χ². Efficiency, position and alignment do not move at all.

Two things are true at once: the bench data prefer the inverted kernel inside this model, and the inverted kernel cannot be a physical resistive film. So the preference is evidence that the model is wrong in that direction, not that the film is. The failure is also plane-specific — the corrected kernel improves X on both detectors and degrades Y on both, and Y is the plane the kernel acts on. A single global ratio is what fails; a per-plane ratio, pinned on X and bounded-free on Y, is the identified next experiment. Gate table and per-detector χ² cost: mx_june_wft/R06_GATE_2026-08-19.md; the retirement itself: mx_june_wft/RETIRE_C2GTC1_2026-08-21.md.

Anyone who reads c2 > c1 off a slide will ask how charge reaches the second neighbour without passing the first, and there is no answer. That is why the worse number ships.

11Does it work

The reference telescope never enters any of the above. Held-out events — the ones the calibration did not train on — put the fitted angle against M3.

The bottom-right panel is the check that cannot be tuned away. Divide the fitted w by the reference angle and you get an implied drift velocity; if the model were mistiming the ladder, that number would depend on track angle. Across three bins it varies by 1.2 (X) and 0.7 (Y) µm/ns against a per-bin uncertainty of about 0.7 — flat within what 220 events can say, and no more than that. The full run has the statistics to say it properly: spread 1.1 (X) and 1.4 (Y) µm/ns around the calibrated 36.6. Re-running that check on the corrected bundle is part of the re-freeze. The per-strip hit-time chain, on identical events, sweeps 13 µm/ns across the same bins.

The position panel is not a detector resolution: σ68 ≈ 628 µm is dominated by M3 pointing and by multiple scattering of a few-GeV cosmic between the telescope and the chamber. The detector’s position resolution is measured on the SPS beam instead (176 ± 35 µm on det4).

12What this means for the deck

  • The kernel figure on slide 9 has to change. It is drawn from the frozen bundle and therefore shows c2 > c1. It should be drawn from the corrected constants — which is a one-line change in make_share.py, since it reads the bundle rather than hard-coding — and the amplitudes can then be quoted rather than hedged. The “Y shares ~3× more than X” line is measured (2.9×) and stays.
  • Slides 9b and 9c should be regenerated on the corrected bundle too, so the deck does not carry two different kernels in one section. The angle numbers do not move (section 10), so no caption arithmetic changes — but slide 9c’s event display will shift by one depth bin, which is fine and worth knowing before someone compares screenshots.
  • Slide 9c’s denominator is wrong independently of all this: it attributes σ68 = 1.19°/1.16° to “the full 7,093-event run”. 7,093 is the number of reconstructed events; the resolution is measured on the 6,852 (X) and 6,850 (Y) that also have an M3 reference.
  • None of the deck’s physics numbers move — efficiency, angle resolution, the implied-velocity check are all unchanged within errors. What changes is that the calibration behind them becomes describable.

The full re-freeze — swap the manifest to calib_bundle_r06, re-run the reco, re-measure w0/kw, re-run the digest — was done on 21 August as a condor campaign. Details in the sharing kernel, measured note.
